source.example_name: d12r6 (driver for routine CONVLV) -- FFT convolution vs direct-method 'Expected'

problem.domain: 1-D, n=16 samples, cyclic (periodic) convolution via FFT (four1 + realft + twofft chain)
problem.rhs_or_ic_formula: data[i]=1.0 for 6<=i<=10 (i.e. n/2-n/8 .. n/2+n/8), else 0.0 (16 values, 1-based); respns[i]=1.0 for 3<=i<=6, else 0.0 (m=9, 1-based, NR wrap-around lag convention); ans = cyclic convolution of data with respns

params._note: Expected values are the example's exact direct-convolution result (book's own cmp[] loop), integer-valued and hand-verifiable; reproduced by independent NumPy FFT cyclic convolution to <1e-12 (Python cross-check 2026-06-17). Bare four1 ships NO printed numeric table in the Example Book; convlv is the FFT-family example whose expected output is exactly determined by the book's specified input + direct method.

expected.printed_precision_sig_figs: exact (integer-valued convolution; book prints :15:6 / :12:6 but the values are exact integers)
expected._gate_note: Tight gate: expected values are exact integers; backend error is FFT round-off only (~1e-12 at n=16). 1e-6 is conservative headroom.
